children: largest holder plans to vote against nominees from Oasis Management at the company's annual meeting in December.
Billionaire Ron Baron, of Baron Capital, who has been a 30-year holder of Vail Resorts
and has an 18% stake, said he will vote for Vail Resorts' nominees, not the nominees the dissident Oasis has put forward.
Baron's comments come as Oasis is pursuing strategic changes at Vail Resorts (

) and board representation and could propose a sale of the entire company or some of its resorts. Last month, the activist nominated former Disney CEO Robert Chapek, Ashton Hudson, Bryce Roberts, and former Olympic skier Picabo Street to the Vail Resorts board. Oasis has a 9% stake in Vail.

The ski resort operator has been contending with Park City local and billionaire Matthew Prince, who has been pushing Vail to sell him Park City Mountain Resort since last spring. Prince, the CEO, and co-founder of Cloudflare
, told the Colorado Post in June that activist investors have been calling him.
"I do not believe the Oasis nominees would serve the best long-term interests of investors and strongly oppose their candidacies," Baron said in a

to holders on Friday. "I also have serious concerns about Oasis' coordination with Matthew Prince. I believe Prince's self-interested demand that the Company sell him Park City, one of its most iconic mountains, is short-sighted and destructive to long-term shareholder value."
The annual meeting is set for Dec. 14.
Shares of Vail Resorts ticked lower by 0.7% on Friday.

title: Vail Resorts' larger holder, Baron Capital, plans to vote against Oasis nominees
